item.title: The players of the game from Ohio State’s 28-19 win over Northwestern
item.description: COLUMBUS, OH - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith #4 celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio on November 14, 2026. (Photo by Jason Mowry/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ohio State was able to snap their two-game losing streak, beating Northwestern 28-19 on Saturday afternoon in Columbus. The performance wasn’t exactly smooth over 60 minutes, but after suffering defeats against USC and Indiana, the Buckeyes are just happy to get back in the win column. The win by Ohio State was their 36th in the last 37 meetings with Northwestern, and the 12th in a row by the Buckeyes over the Wildcats. There were a number of Ohio State players who had strong performances in the win over Northwestern. Players on the defensive side of the football who have had to deal with some criticism of their play over the last few weeks rebounded on Saturday, while it was obvious the Buckeyes put an emphasis on getting the football into the hands of their best players when the offense was on the field. Before we turn our attention to the final road game of the regular season against Nebraska, we are going to highlight Ohio State’s best players in Saturday’s win over Northwestern. Jeremiah Smith Early on it was obvious the game plan for the Ohio State offense was to get the football into the hands of Jeremiah Smith. Across the first three drives for the Buckeye offense, Smith not only hauled in seven passes, the junior also drew his first pass interference penalty of the season as Ohio State was knocking on the door of the end zone with just under four minutes left in the second quarter. With being targeted frequently early, Smith was able to break the Big Ten career receiving yardage record in the first half, passing John Standeford of Purdue. Smith now has 3,875 career receiving yards, which passes Corey Davis of Western Michigan for the most by a receiver through their first three seasons of their collegiate career. Not only is Smith the only Ohio State receiver to reach 3,000 yards in their career, he will likely finish his college career with over 4,000 yards receiving. Smith extended Ohio State’s lead to 15 points with just over six minutes left in the fourth quarter when he caught a 10-yard touchdown pass from Luke Fahey. The score was the 42nd receiving touchdown for Smith, which gives him the most by an FBS receiver through their freshman, sophomore, and junior seasons. Along with adding to the records he has broken as a Buckeye, Smith also stayed in the Heisman Trophy conversation with his performance against Northwestern. Bo Jackson After rushing for 1,000 yards as a freshman, Bo Jackson continued to work his way to a second consecutive season hitting quadruple digits on the ground. On Saturday the sophomore running back eclipsed 100 yards rushing for the third time in the last five games.

item.title: Littler beats Greaves to start Grand Slam defence
item.description: Luke Littler beat Luke Humphries in the 2025 Grand Slam of Darts final and became world number one for the first time [Getty Images] Luke Littler started his Grand Slam of Darts title defence with a comfortable win over Beau Greaves on the opening night in Wolverhampton. The 19-year-old cruised past Greaves with a 5-2 victory, finishing with an average just under 110 and seven 180s. The world number one raced to a 3-0 lead before calmly withstanding Greaves' threat of a fightback in the best-of-nine match. Littler is unbeaten in 15 Grand Slam matches, and is aiming to become the third player after Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen to win three successive titles. "I am happy with the win," Littler told Sky Sports. "I said in my pre-match interview I needed to get off to a strong start because Beau started to find it at the end there. "Beau was fantastic but I am happy with myself and still 100% here in Wolverhampton. "I think it is what I need. Obviously the past three or four majors haven't gone well, but I have been practising and I am glad I have shown it." Last month, Littler was knocked out in the quarter-finals of the European Championship after he was also beaten in the semis at the World Youth Championships . The expanded tournament sees 48 group stage matches being played across the opening three days. Luke Humphries, who won the World Grand Prix title in October, beat Paolo Nebrida to begin his campaign while fellow Englishman and two-time major winner Ross Smith suffered a shock 5-3 defeat by youngster Rusty-Jake Rodriguez. English debutant Henry Coates, 20, held his own against Van Gerwen but the three-time champion won the deciding leg to clinch a 5-4 win. There were also wins for Gerwyn Price, Nathan Aspinall, Stephen Bunting and Dutchman Gian van Veen. item.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka will be replaced as world number two by Mirra Andreeva on Monday [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. item.title: Svitolina races in WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva
item.description: Elina Svitolina is a three-time finalist at the WTA Finals [Getty Images] Elina Svitolina dropped just three games as she thrashed Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva. Ukraine's Svitolina was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes. It caps a remarkable turnaround for world number six Svitolina in Indian Wells, having suffered a heavy defeat in her opening group match against Andreeva. However, she has shown all of her fighting spirit to win her next three matches, including snapping a six-match losing streak to Aryna Sabalenka on Friday. Svitolina now has 11 wins over top-10 opponents this year - the most of any player on the WTA Tour. "After losing the first match I was ready to go home, and now I'm in the final," the 32-year-old said. "I will do my homework with my coaches - I will try to win a bit more games than I did in the first match [against Andreeva]." Svitolina is back in the world's top 10 for the first time since October 2021. She took maternity leave in May 2022 to have daughter Skai, and has made an effort to play more aggressive tennis since her return. She returned brilliantly against Noskova, neutralising the Czech's big serve from the first game. Noskova was well below her best, hitting 11 double faults and committing 27 unforced errors to Svitolina's 18. It is the third time Svitolina has reached the final of the season-ending tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018. Earlier, Andreeva became the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece with a composed victory over Jessica Pegula. French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4. The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004. Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two. "I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight. "But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy." Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets. The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon. She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula. Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite. item.title: Christian Pulisic's brace powers USMNT to 6-0 rout of Haiti in Mauricio Pochettino's farewell tour
item.description: MIAMI — The U.S. found itself Saturday inside a handsome stadium that usually showcases Lionel Messi, taking instruction from a coach who is abandoning it for Manchester United and playing an away match on home soil because the opponent wasn’t allowed to host. All the peculiarities of the day manifested themselves into a riotous result: USA 6, Haiti 0. In Mauricio Pochettino’s penultimate match before leaving for England, the Americans gave a ruthless performance in the first leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals at Nu Stadium. In his first appearance since the World Cup, Christian Pulisic recorded his first two-goal game for the U.S. in 3 ½ years as the U.S. all but secured its place in the semifinals next spring. The second leg — and Pochettino’s farewell — is Tuesday in Cincinnati. Saturday was designated the Haitian home leg, but because of ongoing security issues in Port-au-Prince, the Haitians were forced to play elsewhere. Initially scheduled for Kingston, Jamaica — the venue for Haiti’s two home matches in September — the first leg was moved to Miami to take advantage of the large Haitian diaspora in South Florida. Coming off its first World Cup appearance since 1974 — and with a supportive audience — Haiti saw a massive opportunity to get the upper hand on CONCACAF elite. A three-time champion, the U.S. is seeking its fifth trip to the Nations League semifinals in five attempts. The final four will take place in late March at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles. The Americans were coming off the high of a four-match sweep in the September-October window. Those were friendlies, though. The Nations League is an official competition, with an automatic berth in next summer’s Gold Cup at stake. Pochettino’s roster was incomplete following the injury withdrawals of midfielder Gio Reyna last weekend and right back Sergiño Dest on Thursday. However, with Pulisic, Balogun and Weston McKennie back for the first time since the World Cup, the U.S. possessed the power to get past Haiti. Christian Pulisic made up for lost time Saturday, scoring twice in less than two minutes during the USMNT's 6-0 rout of Haiti. item.title: Cortland stays perfect with Cortaca Jug win vs. Ithaca at Yankee Stadium
item.description: SUNY Cortland kept its unbeaten record intact with a 30-23 victory over rival Ithaca College on Saturday, Nov. 14 in the second Cortaca Jug football game played at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Announced attendance for the 67th Cortaca Jug game was 31,118. Cortland will take a 10-0 record into the NCAA Division III playoffs after cutting Ithaca's lead in the all-time series to 44-37-3. Ithaca, a 26-21 winner over Cortland in last year's meeting, closed its season with a 7-3 mark. Red Dragons quarterback Mike Rescigno accounted for four touchdowns in Saturday's victory. He completed 11-of-19 passes for 217 yards and two touchdowns to go with 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries. Jayson Zeva caught four passes for 115 yards for Cortland. Sam Cotton had four catches for 53 yards, including touchdowns that covered 12 and 20 yards. Rescigno scored on a 19-yard run with 12 minutes, 42 seconds remaining to help the Red Dragons increase their lead to 30-20. Cortland led 23-13 at halftime. Ithaca quarterback Michael Reed completed 16-of-24 passes for 283 yards and three touchdowns. Reed connected with Tian Murray for first-half touchdowns of 59 and 27 yards, the only catches for Murray. Reed added a 22-yard TD pass to Colin Schumm to bring the Bombers within 23-20 eight seconds into the fourth quarter. Union-Endicott graduate Nicholas Lang caught six passes for 87 yards for Ithaca. Andrew Rice kicked a 19-yard field goal with 8:26 remaining to cut Cortland's lead to 30-23. Cortland's defense had five sacks, led by two from George Gjelaj. His first sack led to a safety that opened the scoring. His second, on fourth-and-5 with just over a minute to play, ended Ithaca's final drive at the Bombers' 15-yard line. With the sacks a big part of it, Ithaca was limited to 57 rushing yards on 34 attempts. The selection show for the 40-team NCAA Division III playoffs is scheduled for 5 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15. Cortland has an automatic berth as champion of the Empire 8. This article originally appeared on Ithaca Journal: Cortland stays perfect with Cortaca Jug win vs. Ithaca at Yankee Stadium

item.title: What placing TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activating Greg Van Roten and Reggie Gilliam means for the Patriots
item.description: At around 10 p.m. local time in Germany on Saturday, the New England Patriots announced that they have made some changes to their roster . Running back TreVeyon Henderson was headed to injured reserve due to the illness that has kept him out since late October, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten were both activated from IR. With the Patriots having entered the weekend at 52 players on their roster, Saturday’s transactions meant that they now have a full complement of players available again. What else do the moves mean, though? Let’s find out. RB TreVeyon Henderson: Placed on IR TreVeyon Henderson taking to social media last Friday already was an ominous sign. In a statement addressing the illness that had kept him out for more than a week at that point, he mentioned that “my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions” were affected by the “unexpected and unusual medical emergency” he had been dealing with. While there might still have been hope at that point that he would be able to return in a relatively short period of time, Saturday’s move means that that will not be the case. Henderson will be out for at least the next four games, starting with the upcoming contest against the Detroit Lions. Other games he is now slated to miss include matchups with the Chargers, Bills and Vikings. He is eligible to return to practice and off injured reserve ahead of the Patriots’ Week 15 game in Kansas City, even though an obvious question mark hangs over that comeback given the most recent information we have available — information, head coach Mike Vrabel also did not add to this week. “I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back,” he said on Thursday at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. “When that is I don’t know. I don’t have a timetable, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how he’s doing.” From a football perspective, Henderson going to IR officially removes the No. 2 running back from the Patriots’ active roster. This leaves the group looking as follows: 53-man roster (3): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), Corey Kiner (9 | KR), Lan Larison (34) Practice squad (1): Terrell Jennings (26) IR (2): Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending), TreVeyon Henderson (32) Rhamondre Stevenson is the clear top option, something that would not change with Henderson available. He is the Patriots’ most reliable back in all aspects of playing the position, and by far their best pass protector at the position. Still, Henderson as a rotational second option would bring a more dynamic element to the table than the likes of Corey Kiner and Lan Larison. That element is now missing, even though Kiner in particular has had some promising moments as of late and given Stevenson’s unclear outlook — he is questionable with a knee injury — might see increased reps versus Detroit. item.description: “He just has a presence.” Former Pittsburgh Penguins coach Eddie Olczyk made the prescient remark about the team’s first-round pick and first-overall pick, Marc-Andre Fleury , when recounting Fleury’s first professional game. The moment occurred on Oct. 10, 2003, when a Pittsburgh Penguins crowd starving for good news got their first glimpse of what was to come. Goalie Marc-Andre Fleury made his NHL debut as a remarkably athletic, bright-yellow-pad-wearing, big, toothy, grinning goalie. He made 46 of 48 saves and kept the downtrodden Penguins in the game against the LA Kings in a 3-0 loss. To finish a two-on-one, LA star Ziggy Palffy had a yawning cage and snapped it toward the net from the left wing … and then there was a leg pad to steal the goal. The Civic Arena crowd erupted. Fleury was the first brick in the championship core, and that hope sprang eternal. It took six more years, a couple of coaches, and a new general manager before those Stanley Cup dreams came to fruition, and it took another impressive Fleury save to secure what became a dynasty. Saturday, the Penguins inducted Fleury into the team’s Hall of Fame. “It’s always fun coming back for any reason. I feel like I’ve been back many, many times, but I love this team. It still feels like my team,” said Fleury Saturday. “You know, the organization gave me a chance to live my dream, right, and play here for so long. So to me, it means a lot that they were taking the time to recognize me and bring me back for today.” The Penguins also inducted the general manager who built the second championship chapter of the Penguins dynasty, Jim Rutherford . Rutherford assumed the duties of a flailing organization that had careened into chaos after firing GM Ray Shero , and a shady delay in firing coach Dan Bylsma tarnished their reputation in 2014. Potential GM candidates balked at the organization’s offers. And even after Rutherford was hired, potential coaches weren’t interested in joining the mess. Of course, the team still had Sidney Crosby , Evgeni Malkin , Kris Letang , and Fleury, but a string of disastrous playoff losses and internal tensions created an undesirable situation. (Provided by Brent Warzocha/UAlbany Athletics) ALBANY - Up against a University at Albany football team determined to start fast and considering Great Danes head coach Tom Perkovich's stellar record on Senior Day, the University of Maine never stood much of a chance on Saturday afternoon. They remained in the discussion for an at-large bid to the Football Championship Subdivision playoffs heading into next week's regular-season finale at North Carolina A&T. UAlbany scored touchdowns on its first three possessions to take a 21-0 lead over Maine, a turnaround from the 28-0 halftime deficit the Great Danes faced at Bryant. item.description: Steelers waive 27-game cornerback. Getty Steelers waive cornerback Terrell Smith. Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers made a defensive move ahead of their game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Pittsburgh is set to go on the road to play the Bengals in a pivotal AFC North showdown on Sunday Night Football, in a battle for first place in the division. The Steelers are 3.5-point underdogs on the road. Pittsburgh Steelers Waive Terrell Smith Getty Steelers waive cornerback Terrell Smith. Steelers activated DT Derrick Harmon from injured reserve and waived CB Terell Smith. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 14, 2026 “Steelers activated DT Derrick Harmon from injured reserve and waived CB Terell Smith,” Adam Schefter wrote on X . Smith played college football at Minnesota. He was selected in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Chicago Bears . He had a solid rookie season, recording 49 tackles, 1 forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 12 games, including four starts. Smith then played in 14 games in 2024, including two starts, recording 19 tackles, four passes defensed, and an interception. He suffered a torn patellar tendon during preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve. After missing the entire 2025 season, Smith was cut as part of final roster cuts and signed with the Washington Commanders ‘ practice squad.
